message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians will enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a 3‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 | Sun | **Dec 30 – Jan 1** (Sat‑Sun‑Sun) | The holiday itself is on Sunday, so the weekend is already long. |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, PEI, NB, NS, NL, BC, AB, SK, MB) | Feb 20 | Mon | **Feb 18 – Feb 20** (Sat‑Mon) | Dates vary by province; all listed provinces observe it on the 3rd Monday of February. |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 | Fri | **Apr 7 – Apr 9** (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Federal holiday; observed nationwide. |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 | Mon | **May 20 – May 22** (Sat‑Mon) | Celebrates Queen Victoria’s birthday; observed by most provinces. |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 | Sat | **Jul 1 – Jul 3** (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) | Since the holiday falls on Saturday, it’s observed on Monday, July 2. |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 | Mon | **Sep 2 – Sep 4** (Sat‑Mon) | Nationwide federal holiday. |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 | Mon | **Oct 7 – Oct 9** (Sat‑Mon) | Observed by all provinces. |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 | Mon | **Nov 9 – Nov 11** (Sat‑Mon) | Observed nationwide; some provinces give a statutory holiday. |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 | Mon | **Dec 23 – Dec 25** (Sat‑Mon) | The holiday falls on Monday, so the preceding weekend is part of the long weekend. |

### Quick Tips for Your App

1. **Province‑specific holidays** – Family Day dates differ by province; you may want to allow users to select their province so the correct date is shown.
2. **Observed dates** – When a holiday falls on a weekend (e.g., Canada Day on Saturday), the statutory holiday is usually observed on the following Monday. Make sure your calendar logic accounts for this.
3. **Optional holidays** – Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in BC). If you want to support those, add a configuration per province.

Feel free to copy the table into your holiday‑planning app or use the data to generate dynamic calendars. Happy planning!
